anchor.statement: Lemma 5.1. There exists an interval 0 ≤ ξ ≤ a, ξ = √ X, extending from the axis into the inner collar of Theorem 4.6(i), where the stress cone inequalities hold with a uniform positive margin, on which every positive order has a unique solution of Equations (5.2) to (5.6) with ϕ n (0, η ) = U n (0, η ) = Π n (0, η ) = 0. The profiles are smooth in X and, for each fixed radial derivative, holomorphic on a neighborhood of [−1, 1] in the parameter η . That neighborhood and its bounds may depend on the order and the radial derivative; a does not. Uniqueness holds among solutions whose profiles extend holomorphically in η to a neighborhood of [−1, 1], with bounds uniform for 0 ≤ ξ ≤ a. The zero axis values leave the leading traces of ϕ , U, and Π unchanged by every positive- order coefficient.

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: exists_local_slow_hierarchy gives a solution of every positive order on one radial interval and one complex parameter set, with zero axis values; positive_solution_unique gives uniqueness for the first-order system (5.7) for given coefficient data. That the interval of the actual hierarchy reaches into the inner collar, and that the stress cone holds there 'with a uniform positive margin', follow only by combining analyticEnd_lt_radius, window_order and trueWidth_spec (the cone holds pointwise on a collar) with a compactness argument that no declaration states; identifying positive_solution_unique's system with each order of nominalHierarchy is also the reader's step.
